disclosures.name: TestCertCache
disclosures.signature: timed out waiting for expected ref count
disclosures.reason: The test nils its own local and then asserts, from inside the same still-running frame, that the object it dropped has become collectible: `certA = nil; runtime.GC()`, then a four-second poll for the cache entry's reference count to fall from 2 to 1, ending in this t.Fatal. The finalizer that would decrement it works — runtime.SetFinalizer is the hand-owned ConditionalWeakTable-and-sentinel bridge, runtime.GC() is Collect then WaitForPendingFinalizers then Collect, and sync's banked TestPoolGC measures 98 of 100 objects finalizing on the first try — but `certA, err := cc.newCert(p.Bytes)` is a two-result call whose results materialize an address-exposed frame temp, and an address-exposed slot is not lifetime-tracked: the CLR reports it live for the whole method, so the activeCert stays reachable until TestCertCache RETURNS and the count cannot fall while the test is looking. Measured to fail at the FIRST check identically in a separately built optimized Release host, so it is the CLR's GC-info conservatism rather than the non-optimizing JIT's frame-wide liveness. Same mechanism, and the same non-satisfiable-at-any-layer-go2cs-owns conclusion, as sync's TestOnceXGC and TestPoolGC disclosures.

disclosures.name: TestBogoSuite
disclosures.reason: The test delegates to BoringSSL's own test runner, spawned as `go test .` in the boringssl module — a child that carries Go's default 10-minute test-binary deadline, which neither the package's code nor the host controls (the test passes no -timeout, in either language). Inside that wall the runner spawns the shim once per case — 5,481 spawns in this configuration — and the shim IS the converted test host: since 2026-08-27 a self-contained single-file executable (the shape that retired the class's relocatable-executable entry), whose process start (bundle open, CLR startup, JIT over the converted-stdlib closure) measures 2.61 s where Go's statically linked test binary starts in 0.038 s -- the framework-dependent shape this entry was minted against measured 3.30 s, so the single-file publish bought ~0.7 s and the ~69x that remains is structural to the deployment shape. The ReadyToRun rung was measured 2026-08-28 (the empty-the-class commission): R2R composite publish (+161 s, 181.5 MB) cuts shim startup to 0.74 s, and driven DIRECTLY with the wall lifted the runner completes the whole configuration -- 3,242 cases, 861 PASS / 2,381 allow-unimplemented SKIP, ZERO failures, ok end to end -- in 1,316 s against the 600 s wall the test itself carries: 2.2x over on this 6-core host, down from ~20x. The wall is now THROUGHPUT-bound, not startup-bound: at the measured slot cost the zero-startup (AOT) floor computes to ~980 s here, so no startup work alone clears it on this host class -- the entry retires when managed steady-state TLS throughput on the sweep host crosses the runner's own deadline, and the interop itself is no longer in question at any width — it is what the artifact IS, not how far an implementation has got. Measured 2026-08-18: the runner reaches ~267 of 5,481 cases at its wall even with 16 parallel shim workers — a ~20x shortfall no deadline the test can express would close — then exits without writing its results JSON, which selects exactly the failure arm this signature pins. The TLS interop capability itself is not in question and is proven by value in the same suite: with `-bogo-filter Client-Verify-ECDSA-TLS1` the converted host completes a TLS handshake with certificate verification against BoringSSL as the peer, PASS in 14 s end to end including the module download and runner build. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-29 on a second box (i9), and this is the first measurement whose numbers are produced by GO'S CONTRACT rather than partly by a harness defect: 861 PASS / 2,381 SKIP / 0 FAIL, exit 0 — identical to the record above on all three buckets — wall 1,046.3 s, about 20% faster than this box and still not crossing the 600 s deadline. What changed underneath it: the arc exposed two ordering defects in the converted test HOST, and before they were fixed 1,902 of these cases failed on a flag-parse ordering bug rather than on anything about TLS (the host ruled on an unrecognized flag before the package's TestMain could install the flag.Usage that exits 89, which BoGo reads as unimplemented-and-skip; and the host's own parse ran before TestMain at all). So the disclosed shape was partly an artifact of the harness, and is no longer: the suite now executes exactly the cases Go executes and skips exactly the ones Go skips. Same verdict, entirely different evidence. The partition is also now known to be contract-determined and load-INVARIANT — 861 runnable / 2,381 skipped held across four runs on two machines under roughly 4x differing timeout pressure, with contention moving tests only inside the runnable set and never across the skip boundary — so a future re-measure that reports a different split is reporting a real change, not noise. Retirement condition unchanged and sharper for it: this entry retires when managed steady-state TLS throughput on the sweep host crosses the runner's own 600 s deadline. Same self-retiring texture as os/exec's relocatable-single-file entries: publish the host with fast startup (ReadyToRun/AOT) and this row starts passing, the disclosed count stops matching, and the sweep fails until the entry is removed. SECOND ENVIRONMENTAL ARM (2026-08-28, the bogo skip-parity lane): the signature above is `bogo_shim_test.go:414` — the arm taken when the runner RAN and outlived its own deadline. A host that never had the BoringSSL module does not reach it; it dies fifty lines earlier at `bogo_shim_test.go:364`, `failed to download boringssl`, and GO DIES THERE TOO, identically, at the same line, for the same reason — measured by pointing GOMODCACHE at an empty directory with GOPROXY=off, where both runtimes report `--- FAIL: TestBogoSuite (0.61s)` off that one line. Until that arm was admitted (`hostConditionalSignature`) the comparison called the converted side MOVED and crypto/tls could not validate AT ALL on such a host: `TestBogoSuite: Go="fail" C#="fail" (failure does not match the disclosed host-limit signature "bogo failed: exit status 1")`. It is admitted ONLY in the host-conditional fail/fail shape, where Go itself failed the same way and the converted side is provably not the half that moved; in the Go pass / C# fail shape the primary signature still governs alone. NOTE this does NOT retire the entry, and the same lane measured why: the entry's retirement condition is the throughput one above, and on a capability-PRESENT host that misses the runner's 600 s wall — the i7-5820K, 2026-08-28, 400 matched + 2 disclosed against a banked 3643 + 1, its Go side fanning out all 3,242 BoGo rows in 50-66 s — the pinned Go pass / C# fail divergence is exactly as live as the day it was written. Retiring it there would convert a measured divergence into an undisclosed one.
disclosures.hostConditional: The GO side is decided by network reachability of the pinned boringssl module, which `go test` downloads and builds BoringSSL's own runner from, and by how far that runner gets inside the 10-minute deadline Go's test binary carries by default — so per host and per run the Go baseline passes, expands into its 3,243-row case matrix, or fails.
